title_en: Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Justice, and Ministry of Public Security — Several Supplementary Provisions on Lawyers' Participation in Litigation
full_text_en:
**Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate**

**Ministry of Justice             Ministry of Public Security**

**Several Supplementary Provisions on Lawyers' Participation in Litigation**

(86) Si Fa Gong Zi No. 196

To the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), Justice Departments (Bureaus), and Lawyers Associations of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; and for forwarding to People's Courts at all levels, People's Procuratorates at all levels, Public Security Organs at all levels and detention houses, prisons, Justice Bureaus (Sections) at all levels, and Law Firms (Legal Advisory Offices) at all levels:

On April 27, 1981, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice issued the "Joint Circular on Several Specific Provisions Concerning Lawyers' Participation in Litigation," which played a positive role in ensuring that lawyers smoothly carry out their tasks and perform their work of participating in court proceedings. In order to enable lawyers to better play their role in litigation activities, and in accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)," and the "Interim Regulations on Lawyers of the People's Republic of China," the following supplementary provisions are hereby made on specific issues concerning lawyers' participation in litigation:

1. Written evidence, defense statements, and representation statements formally submitted by a lawyer to the People's Court must be placed in the case file by the People's Court. Opinions and other materials related to the case shall also be appended to the file if the People's Court deems it necessary.

2. Where the People's Court considers it necessary, it may itself investigate and verify the evidentiary materials provided by the lawyer, or send them to the investigative organs for investigation and verification, for reference when deciding the case.

3. The People's Court shall notify lawyers to appear in court to perform their duties by means of a notice; it shall not summon lawyers by subpoena. Lawyers shall appear in court in accordance with the notice of the People's Court and perform their duties according to law, and shall not unreasonably obstruct the normal conduct of litigation.

4. When a lawyer appears in court to perform duties according to law, he shall strictly abide by the rules and order of the court, and strictly observe and implement the litigation procedures prescribed by law. Judicial personnel in the court shall respect and protect the lawyer's right to perform his duties in court according to law, and shall not arbitrarily order the lawyer to withdraw from the courtroom.

5. In any case in which a lawyer participates in litigation, the People's Court shall list the lawyer's name in the judgment or ruling of the case.

6. In accordance with Article 2, Paragraph (3) of the "Interim Regulations on Lawyers of the People's Republic of China," a lawyer may accept the entrustment of the victim of a public prosecution case and his close relatives to serve as an agent ad litem to participate in litigation. The lawyer acting as agent ad litem for the victim shall closely cooperate with the procurator acting as the public prosecutor. During the court trial, the lawyer acting as agent ad litem for the victim may, with the permission of the presiding judge, ask questions and answer questions during the court investigation, and state the opinions of the represented party to the court, so as to fully safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of the victim.

June 26, 1986

For the convenience of readers in understanding the spirit of this document, the "Joint Circular on Several Specific Provisions Concerning Lawyers' Participation in Litigation" of the two courts and two ministries dated April 27, 1981 is hereby appended to this document and published together.

**Supreme People's Court  Supreme People's Procuratorate  Ministry of Public Security  Ministry of Justice**

**Joint Circular on Several Specific Provisions Concerning Lawyers' Participation in Litigation**

(81) Fa Yan Zi No. 6

(81) Gao Jian Fa (Xing) No. 14

(81) Gong Fa (Yan) No. 41

(81) Si Fa Gong Zi No. 43

To the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), Justice Departments (Bureaus), and Lawyers Associations of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; and for forwarding to People's Courts at all levels, People's Procuratorates at all levels, Public Security Organs at all levels and detention houses, prisons and other custodial places, Justice Bureaus (Sections) at all levels, and Legal Advisory Offices at all levels:

In accordance with the spirit of the relevant provisions of the "Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" and the "Interim Regulations on Lawyers of the People's Republic of China," and for the purpose of ensuring that lawyers can smoothly perform their duties, do a good job of appearing in court to participate in litigation, so as to safeguard the correct implementation of the law and protect the legitimate rights and interests of litigants, the following provisions are hereby made on several issues concerning lawyers' (including part-time lawyers and trainee lawyers; the same below) participation in litigation:

**I. Concerning Inspection of Case Files**

1. A lawyer who serves as a defender or agent ad litem in a criminal case or as an agent ad litem in a civil case may go to the court to inspect the materials of the case he is handling and understand the facts of the case. However, records of the judicial committee and the collegial panel, as well as materials containing leads concerning other cases, shall not be inspected.

2. When a lawyer inspects case files, the court shall provide necessary convenience and provide a place for the lawyer to inspect the files.

3. When inspecting case files, a lawyer may make excerpts. The excerpted materials shall be kept in the files of the legal advisory office.

4. A lawyer shall strictly keep confidential any state secrets and personal privacy encountered during the inspection of case files.

**II. Concerning Meetings with Detained Defendants**

1. A lawyer serving as a defender in a criminal case may, by presenting the work card of the legal advisory office and a special introduction letter with a fixed format, meet with the defendant in a detention house or other custodial place (hereinafter collectively referred to as custodial places). For each meeting, one or two lawyers may go, as determined by the legal advisory office. Other defenders may meet with the detained defendant only with the permission of the court and upon holding a special introduction letter from the court.

2. When a lawyer or other defender permitted by the court meets with a detained defendant, the custodial place shall provide convenience and designate an appropriate meeting room. Where custody is necessary, the custodial personnel shall pay attention to the manner of doing so and try to avoid increasing the defendant's concerns during the conversation; after the meeting, they shall not inquire about the content of the conversation between the defendant and the lawyer or other defender, so as not to affect the defendant's full exercise of the right to defense.

3. When a lawyer or other defender permitted by the court meets with a detained defendant, they shall remain vigilant to strictly prevent incidents such as the defendant's escape, assault, or suicide. After the meeting is concluded, the defendant shall be handed over to the custodial personnel for re-detention in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the custodial place; any matters that need to be known or noted during custody shall be promptly communicated to the custodial place.

**III. Concerning Copies of Litigation Documents**

1. In all public prosecution cases, the People's Procuratorate shall attach one copy of the indictment and forward it to the defending lawyer through the court. In a first-instance case where a lawyer is acting as defender, if the People's Procuratorate files an appeal, it shall also attach a copy of the appeal brief and forward it to the defending lawyer through the court.

2. In any criminal or civil case in which a lawyer participates in litigation, whether at first instance or second instance, the court shall provide the handling lawyer with a copy of the judgment or ruling it renders.

3. Where conditions for printing exist, the lawyer's defense statement shall be submitted to the court and the People's Procuratorate for one copy each to be kept on file.

**IV. Concerning Other Related Matters**

1. In cases involving state secrets or personal privacy that are not heard publicly according to law, the defendant may apply to the court to appoint a lawyer to act as his defender, or may himself entrust a lawyer approved by the director of the legal advisory office to act as his defender; if the defendant requests a person other than a lawyer to serve as defender, the court shall examine and decide whether it is permissible.

2. When a court schedules a trial date for opening a case, it shall leave sufficient time for the lawyer to prepare for appearance. If the lawyer considers that the trial date is too early due to the complexity of the case, he may apply to the court for an adjournment, and the court shall consider this within the time limit not affecting the statutory conclusion of the case.

3. After a case has been opened for trial, if the trial is adjourned and continued on another date, the court shall also promptly notify the handling lawyer before the next hearing.

4. Before a criminal judgment or ruling becomes legally effective, if the legal advisory office deems it necessary, it may directly send a defending lawyer to the custodial place to meet with the defendant and inquire about his opinions on the judgment or ruling.

5. In criminal or civil cases tried by a court in which a lawyer serves as an agent ad litem, the court shall not, during the trial, inquire about the lawyer's name, age, place of origin, address, or occupation. A seat shall be provided for the lawyer in the courtroom.

6. A lawyer participating in litigation (including participating in mediation or arbitration activities) may, by presenting the introduction letter of the legal advisory office, visit relevant units or individuals to investigate the facts of the case, and the relevant units and individuals shall provide support.

The above circular is expected to be diligently implemented.

April 27, 1981
